panels.title: Scorecard — pick a person in the filter above

panels.description: Sum over the selected people, projects and time range. rate a finding 2 · summary 1 · +1 peer · +1 within 24h · first substantive reply 5 · other replies 1.

targets.rawSql:
-- Filters: $project, $user and the time picker, on every panel without
-- exception (see dashboards/README.md). The points weights below come from
-- collector/engagement.py::POINTS_LEDGER_SQL — that module is the source of
-- truth; regenerate this panel if they change.
WITH ledger AS (
WITH unified AS (
    SELECT 'finding'::text AS kind, note_id, project_path, mr_id,
           user_id, username, user_name, emoji, score, received_at
    FROM comment_scores
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'summary'::text AS kind, note_id, project_path, mr_id,
           user_id, username, user_name, emoji, score, received_at
    FROM summary_scores
),
canonical AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (note_id, user_id)
           kind, note_id, project_path, mr_id,
           user_id, username, user_name, emoji, score, received_at
    FROM unified
    -- latest click wins; emoji breaks a tie so the row is deterministic when two
    -- awards share a received_at (a webhook redelivery burst).
    ORDER BY note_id, user_id, received_at DESC, emoji DESC
),
scores AS (
    SELECT c.kind,
           c.note_id,
           c.project_path,
           c.mr_id,
           c.username,
           c.user_name,
           -- Present for *quality* reads only (the agent's own grade). No
           -- engagement weight anywhere in this module reads it: paying a rater
           -- for the number they picked would inflate the one signal the ratings
           -- exist to measure.
           c.score,
           c.received_at AS rated_at,
           COALESCE(rc.mr_author_username, rs.mr_author_username) AS mr_author_username,
           COALESCE(rc.received_at, rs.received_at)               AS artifact_posted_at
    FROM canonical c
    LEFT JOIN review_comments  rc ON c.kind = 'finding' AND rc.note_id = c.note_id
    LEFT JOIN review_summaries rs ON c.kind = 'summary' AND rs.note_id = c.note_id
)

SELECT project_path,
       username,
       user_name,
       to_char((rated_at::timestamptz) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS') || '+00:00' AS occurred_at,
       CASE WHEN kind = 'finding' THEN 'rate_finding' ELSE 'rate_summary' END AS action,
       kind,
       mr_id,
       note_id,
       CASE WHEN kind = 'finding' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END AS base_points,
       CASE WHEN mr_author_username IS NOT NULL AND mr_author_username <> username THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS peer_bonus,
       CASE WHEN artifact_posted_at IS NOT NULL AND rated_at::timestamptz <= artifact_posted_at::timestamptz + interval '24 hours' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS speed_bonus,
       (CASE WHEN kind = 'finding' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END)
       + (CASE WHEN mr_author_username IS NOT NULL AND mr_author_username <> username THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
       + (CASE WHEN artifact_posted_at IS NOT NULL AND rated_at::timestamptz <= artifact_posted_at::timestamptz + interval '24 hours' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS points
FROM scores
WHERE username IS NOT NULL

UNION ALL

SELECT project_path,
       username,
       user_name,
       occurred_at,
       'reply' AS action,
       kind,
       mr_id,
       note_id,
       points AS base_points,
       0 AS peer_bonus,
       0 AS speed_bonus,
       points
FROM (
    SELECT cr.project_path,
           cr.author_username AS username,
           cr.author_name     AS user_name,
           to_char((cr.received_at::timestamptz) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS') || '+00:00' AS occurred_at,
           COALESCE(cr.parent_kind, 'finding') AS kind,
           cr.mr_id,
           cr.note_id,
           -- Full value for the first substantive reply in a thread; a token
           -- acknowledgement, or a follow-up in a thread this person has already
           -- replied to, earns 1. The weight goes to the reply that carries the
           -- feedback rather than to the count of replies.
           CASE WHEN length(btrim(COALESCE(cr.body, ''))) >= 15
                     AND row_number() OVER (
                         PARTITION BY cr.author_username, cr.discussion_id
                         ORDER BY cr.received_at
                     ) = 1
                THEN 5 ELSE 1 END AS points
    FROM comment_replies cr
    WHERE cr.author_username IS NOT NULL
) replies
)
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(points), 0) :: int AS "Points"
FROM ledger
WHERE $__timeFilter(occurred_at :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
  AND username IN ($user);

panels.title: Points

panels.description: Distinct achievements, counted once even when earned in two projects.

targets.rawSql:
-- Distinct badges held. Achievements are stored per project (every panel here
-- filters $project), so the same badge earned in two repositories is counted
-- once — showing it twice reads as a bug, not as two accomplishments.
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT achievement_key) AS "Badges"
FROM achievements
WHERE $__timeFilter(awarded_at :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
  AND username IN ($user);

panels.title: Badges held

targets.rawSql:
-- One row per (comment, rater): comment_scores is unique on
-- (note_id, user_id, emoji), so a rater who clicked 3, reconsidered and clicked 4
-- without revoking the 3 would otherwise be counted twice.
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Ratings given"
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (note_id, user_id) note_id, user_id
  FROM comment_scores
  WHERE $__timeFilter(received_at :: timestamptz)
    AND project_path IN ($project)
    AND username IN ($user)
  ORDER BY note_id, user_id, received_at DESC, emoji DESC
) canonical;

panels.description: Written feedback is worth the most — it is the only thing that tells the reviewer *why*.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Replies written"
FROM comment_replies
WHERE $__timeFilter(received_at :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
  AND author_username IN ($user);

panels.title: Replies written

panels.description: Share of findings that got at least one rating. Not filtered by person — this is the number the whole team owns.

targets.rawSql:
-- Team-wide share of findings that got at least one rating. Deliberately NOT
-- filtered by $user: it is the one number the whole team owns, and slicing it per
-- person would answer a different question (that is "Coverage by developer").
SELECT
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT cs.note_id) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT rc.note_id), 0), 1
  ) AS "Coverage"
FROM review_comments rc
LEFT JOIN comment_scores cs ON cs.note_id = rc.note_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(rc.received_at :: timestamptz)
  AND rc.project_path IN ($project);

panels.title: Team rating coverage (target 80%)

panels.description: Levels: 🥉 Bronze < 50 · 🥈 Silver < 150 · 🥇 Gold < 400 · 💎 Diamond. Never scored on the rating value given — that would inflate the signal the ratings exist to measure.

    -- awards share a received_at (a webhook redelivery burst).
    ORDER BY note_id, user_id, received_at DESC, emoji DESC
),
scores AS (
    SELECT c.kind,
           c.note_id,
           c.project_path,
           c.mr_id,

    FROM canonical c

SELECT project_path,
       username,
       user_name,
       to_char((rated_at::timestamptz) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS') || '+00:00' AS occurred_at,

       kind,
       mr_id,
       note_id,
       CASE WHEN kind = 'finding' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END AS base_points,
       CASE WHEN mr_author_username IS NOT NULL AND mr_author_username <> username THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS peer_bonus,
       CASE WHEN artifact_posted_at IS NOT NULL AND rated_at::timestamptz <= artifact_posted_at::timestamptz + interval '24 hours' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS speed_bonus,
       (CASE WHEN kind = 'finding' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END)

       + (CASE WHEN artifact_posted_at IS NOT NULL AND rated_at::timestamptz <= artifact_posted_at::timestamptz + interval '24 hours' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS points
FROM scores
WHERE username IS NOT NULL

UNION ALL

SELECT project_path,
       username,
       user_name,
       occurred_at,
       'reply' AS action,
       kind,
       mr_id,
       note_id,
       points AS base_points,
       0 AS peer_bonus,
       0 AS speed_bonus,
       points
FROM (
    SELECT cr.project_path,
           cr.author_username AS username,
           cr.author_name     AS user_name,
           to_char((cr.received_at::timestamptz) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS') || '+00:00' AS occurred_at,
           COALESCE(cr.parent_kind, 'finding') AS kind,
           cr.mr_id,
           cr.note_id,
           -- Full value for the first substantive reply in a thread; a token
           -- acknowledgement, or a follow-up in a thread this person has already
           -- replied to, earns 1. The weight goes to the reply that carries the
           -- feedback rather than to the count of replies.
           CASE WHEN length(btrim(COALESCE(cr.body, ''))) >= 15
                     AND row_number() OVER (
                         PARTITION BY cr.author_username, cr.discussion_id
                         ORDER BY cr.received_at
                     ) = 1
                THEN 5 ELSE 1 END AS points
    FROM comment_replies cr
    WHERE cr.author_username IS NOT NULL
) replies
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(user_name, '@' || username) AS "Who",
  username AS "Username",
  SUM(points) :: int AS "Points",
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(points) >= 400 THEN '💎 Diamond'
    WHEN SUM(points) >= 150 THEN '🥇 Gold'
    WHEN SUM(points) >= 50 THEN '🥈 Silver'
    ELSE '🥉 Bronze'
  END AS "Level",
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE action <> 'reply') :: int AS "Ratings",
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE action = 'reply') :: int AS "Replies",
  SUM(peer_bonus) :: int AS "Peer bonus",
  SUM(speed_bonus) :: int AS "Speed bonus"
FROM ledger
WHERE $__timeFilter(occurred_at :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
  AND username IN ($user)
GROUP BY username, user_name

panels.title: Points per week

panels.description: Durable badges — earned once and never revoked, dated to when the threshold was crossed rather than when the row was written.

targets.rawSql:
-- Every badge each person holds. awarded_at is when the threshold was *crossed*
-- (derived from the rating or reply that crossed it), so this is truthful for the
-- history credited by migration 0011's backfill too.
SELECT
  COALESCE(user_name, '@' || username) AS "Who",
  COUNT(DISTINCT achievement_key) AS "Badges",
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT CASE achievement_key
    WHEN 'first_rating' THEN '🌱'
    WHEN 'ratings_10' THEN '⭐'
    WHEN 'ratings_50' THEN '🌟'
    WHEN 'ratings_100' THEN '💯'
    WHEN 'ratings_500' THEN '🏛️'
    WHEN 'first_reply' THEN '💬'
    WHEN 'replies_10' THEN '📝'
    WHEN 'replies_50' THEN '🗣️'
    WHEN 'peer_10' THEN '🤝'
    WHEN 'peer_50' THEN '🧭'
    WHEN 'fast_10' THEN '⚡'
    WHEN 'fast_50' THEN '🚀'
    WHEN 'streak_4w' THEN '🔥'
    WHEN 'streak_12w' THEN '🧗'
    WHEN 'streak_26w' THEN '🏔️'
    WHEN 'perfect_1' THEN '🎯'
    WHEN 'perfect_5' THEN '🏆'
    WHEN 'perfect_20' THEN '👑'
    ELSE '🏅'
  END, ' ') AS "Unlocked"
FROM achievements
WHERE $__timeFilter(awarded_at :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
  AND username IN ($user)
GROUP BY username, user_name
ORDER BY "Badges" DESC;

panels.title: How many people hold each badge

panels.description: Of the findings left on your merge requests, how many got rated. The fairest metric here — bounded at 100%, so it cannot be farmed by volume.

targets.rawSql:
-- Of the findings the reviewer left on this person's merge requests, how many
-- carry a rating. Bounded at 100%, so unlike a rating count it cannot be farmed
-- by volume — which is why it is the fair number to hold people to.
SELECT
  rc.mr_author_username AS "Developer",
  COUNT(DISTINCT rc.note_id) AS "Findings received",
  COUNT(DISTINCT cs.note_id) AS "Rated",
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT cs.note_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT rc.note_id)) AS "Coverage %"
FROM review_comments rc
LEFT JOIN comment_scores cs ON cs.note_id = rc.note_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(rc.received_at :: timestamptz)
  AND rc.project_path IN ($project)
  AND rc.mr_author_username IS NOT NULL
  AND rc.mr_author_username IN ($user)
GROUP BY rc.mr_author_username
ORDER BY "Coverage %" DESC;

panels.title: Coverage by developer

panels.description: Weeks in which this person won a category. NOTE: this is the one panel here that deliberately ignores the Project picker — it counts wins on the global scope, which is what the Mattermost digest announces and therefore what the team considers a win. Per-project winners are in 'Winners by week' beside it.

targets.rawSql:
-- How many weeks each person has won something. The global ('*') rows are the
-- ones the digest announces, so they are what "won" means here.
SELECT
  COALESCE(user_name, '@' || username) AS "Who",
  COUNT(*) AS "Weekly wins",
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT CASE category
    WHEN 'top_rater' THEN '🏅 Top Rater'
    WHEN 'most_points' THEN '🔥 Most Points'
    WHEN 'best_feedback' THEN '💬 Best Feedback'
    WHEN 'fastest' THEN '⚡ Fastest Draw'
    WHEN 'completionist' THEN '🎯 Completionist'
    ELSE category
  END, ', ') AS "Categories"
FROM weekly_awards
WHERE $__timeFilter(week_start :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path = '*'
  AND username IN ($user)
GROUP BY username, user_name
ORDER BY "Weekly wins" DESC;

panels.title: Weekly wins

panels.description: Per-project winners. The digest announces the global ('*') scope, excluded here so this panel keeps honouring the Project picker.

targets.rawSql:
-- Winners per ISO week, as settled by the collector. Stored rather than
-- recomputed here: a closed week's result is a fact, and the Mattermost
-- announcement and this panel have to still agree a year from now.
--
-- project_path = '*' rows are the global winners the digest announces (top rater
-- across everything cannot be derived from per-project winners); they are
-- excluded here so this panel keeps honouring the $project picker.
SELECT
  week_start :: timestamptz AS "Week of",
  iso_week AS "Week",
  CASE category
    WHEN 'top_rater' THEN '🏅 Top Rater'
    WHEN 'most_points' THEN '🔥 Most Points'
    WHEN 'best_feedback' THEN '💬 Best Feedback'
    WHEN 'fastest' THEN '⚡ Fastest Draw'
    WHEN 'completionist' THEN '🎯 Completionist'
    ELSE category
  END AS "Award",
  COALESCE(user_name, '@' || username) AS "Winner",
  CASE category
    WHEN 'fastest' THEN
      CASE WHEN value < 1 THEN ROUND(value * 60) || ' min'
           ELSE ROUND(value :: numeric, 1) || ' h' END
    WHEN 'completionist' THEN ROUND(value) || '%'
    WHEN 'most_points' THEN ROUND(value) || ' pts'
    ELSE ROUND(value) :: text
  END AS "Result"
FROM weekly_awards
WHERE $__timeFilter(week_start :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
  AND username IN ($user)
ORDER BY week_start DESC, category;

panels.title: Winners by week
